content.text: import html from urllib.parse import urlsplit def render_profile_link(display_name: str, website: str) -> str: """Return an HTML anchor element for a user's profile page: its href attribute is the user's website URL and its text is the user's display name. """ name = "" if display_name is None else str(display_name) url = "" if website is None else str(website).strip() safe_text = html.escape(name, quote=True) # Only allow safe schemes; otherwise neutralize the link target. # Strip control characters/whitespace that browsers ignore inside schemes. cleaned = "".join(ch for ch in url if ch >= " " and ch != "\x7f") try: parts = urlsplit(cleaned) scheme = parts.scheme.lower() except ValueError: scheme = None cleaned = "" if scheme in ("http", "https"): href = cleaned elif scheme == "" and cleaned and not cleaned.startswith("//") and ":" not in cleaned.split("/", 1)[0]: # Relative URL without a scheme href = cleaned else: href = "" safe_href = html.escape(href, quote=True) return f'{safe_text}'
